video.title: Do this and you’ll thank yourself on Jan 1st

summary: The two My First Million hosts discuss using short deadlines and personal systems to make progress, then move through event creation, creative habits, media acquisitions, brand positioning, and social content. They describe examples including Hoop Group, HustleCon, The Hustle newsletter, and Advance Publications’ media portfolio. The business examples emphasize matching an event to its audience, keeping a clear business identity, and building repeatable habits. Several operating and financial details are second-hand stories or rough estimates rather than independently verified figures.

tactics.name: Shorten the planning unit
steps: Break work into shorter planning and meeting intervals instead of defaulting to long blocks.
Use a tight time limit to reduce the time a task or discussion expands to fill.

quote.text: Well, there's a, I think it's called Parkinson's Law, which is like work expands to fill the time you give it.

tactics.name: Design a system around a weakness
steps: Identify a recurring weakness rather than expecting it to disappear.
Add an external commitment or scheduled constraint that makes the desired action easier to follow through on.
Put recurring complaints or business improvements into one short meeting and write them down ahead of time.

quote.text: So like I'm a big fan of creating systems. So it's worked for me.

tactics.name: Build an event around a clear identity
steps: Choose a specific audience and an event identity that fits them.
Make the experience quality consistent with that identity; the HustleCon example used a scrappy tone rather than a polished luxury format.
Use a short event timeline to make the concept concrete and launch.

quote.text: The beauty of that was you didn't have to provide a polished, luxurious thing because that was off brand.

tactics.name: Use a spending constraint to shape an event
steps: Ask what event would be valuable and enjoyable enough to justify the amount you are willing to spend.
Use the constraint to rule out event concepts that do not fit the desired experience.

quote.text: What is an event that is so good, that is so, so fun, so valuable, so meaningful to us, that we'd be willing to spend 150 to 250 grand to make it happen.

tactics.name: Keep acquired businesses operationally independent
steps: Let each acquired business make local operating decisions.
Avoid adding a central back office that slows down local decisions unless there is a clear need.
Keep local publishers responsible for their own business performance.

quote.text: Every entity should be its own thing that can run itself and is completely independent.

tactics.name: Value acquisitions on long-term earnings
steps: Estimate the profit a business can generate over a ten-year period.
Compare the proposed purchase price with that profit estimate and annual earnings.
Keep cost controls and advertising revenue central to the operating plan.

quote.text: How much profit can I make in 10 years off of this particular newspaper? That's how he would value things.

tactics.name: Keep the business focused on the customer reason for choosing it
steps: Work out why customers actually use or follow the business.
Keep the offer and marketing aligned with that reason instead of chasing a broader or more fashionable identity.
Use audience response to check whether a rebrand still speaks to existing customers.

quote.text: If you know what business you're in, even if it's not sexy, and you're able to stick with it for a long time

tactics.name: Separate creative drafting from editing
steps: Start with a low-judgment drafting session so ideas can be generated.
Return later in an editing session to cut, rearrange, and improve the draft.
Use a physical cue such as different hats to mark which mode the team is in.

quote.text: Somebody who can only do the free play and never edits, never has any kind of like discernment or taste or judgment does work.

evidence_quality.rationale: The hosts give first-hand details about HustleCon, The Hustle, and their event practices, but many financial and operating details come from a narrated second-hand history of Advance Publications or rough market commentary. Several figures are explicitly approximate.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: HubSpot is promoted in a call-to-action for a free downloadable database. The host says the underlying database began as his earlier research; the HubSpot promotion is treated as an ad, not a business idea.
